_comment: Topical relevance rules for the digest. Alex's world is interior design; these strip the food, fashion, beauty and deal-of-the-day content the big lifestyle feeds mix in. Tune freely - this file is data, not code. See src/scrapers/topics.py for how it is applied.

_default._rescue_note: rescue_titles override a deny_titles match, never a deny_categories match. A category tag is the outlet's own classification and is trusted; a title keyword is a guess.

Martha Stewart._why: Martha is the brand. 'Celebrity News' here usually means her own kitchen, which is exactly the content Alex wants.

House Beautiful._why: Carried over from the original per-outlet exclusions in rss.py. Those were naive substring matches, so 'star' also killed 'starting' and 'shop' killed 'workshop'. Same intent, now word-boundary anchored.

Forbes._why: Our generated feed has no category tags, and the Forbes real-estate page mixes in general business. Require a design or property term instead.

Luxe Magazine._why: Same: generated feed, no categories, but the source page is already design-only.

Vogue._why: Vogue is a fashion book. Only its design and architecture coverage is relevant.

Mansion Global._why: Read via Google News because the site refuses GitHub's data-centre IPs. Google occasionally surfaces a registration or subscription page rather than an article.
